rules.note: Copy of your passport. If you hold dual citizenship, submit copies of both passports.
Not listed in the official requirements.
Certificates from your previous universities. If not in English, French, Italian or German, add certified translations.
Transcripts from your previous universities. If not in English, French, Italian or German, add certified translations.
Complete CV: education, degrees, awards, positions, publications, teaching and practical experience (for art: exhibitions or concerts).
Letter of motivation, maximum 2 pages: why you want to stay in Switzerland and how it affects your career and plans after the scholarship.
Research scholarships only (not art). Detailed plan with milestones and timeline on the official FCS/ESKAS form, maximum 5 pages including a summary for non-specialists. Submit one proposal only.

Research scholarships only: letter of support from your Swiss academic supervisor, plus the supervisor's short CV (max 2 pages). You must find the supervisor; applications without the letter are excluded.
Two letters. You enter the email addresses of two professors in your field; they upload their letters through the online application system.
Art scholarships only (required there): a PDF with links or QR codes to your work samples. Music: three different styles (composers send scores). Visual arts: three artworks with sketches.
Art scholarships: admission (or admission under review) from a Swiss university of the arts or music is required. PhD via a graduate school: admission confirmation. Individual PhDs do not need it.
Only if you already live in Switzerland: residence permit or registration confirmation. Your entry date must not be earlier than 1 August 2026.

new_kinds.name: Supervisor support letter
new_kinds.description: Letter from the academic supervisor or host institution supporting or accepting the applicant's project.
